The note's own argument is meaning, not operation: 'without the glottal-source model concept, fundamental-frequency has no speech-specific operational meaning' - that is Law 8c sayability. F0's accepted definition is the lowest frequency of a periodic waveform, estimated by time-domain (autocorrelation) and frequency-domain (cepstral, peak-picking) methods that all compute identically with or without the glottal-source model. Remove the model and F0 still operates - pitch trackers, ToBI annotation, and musical pitch tracking do not need speech production theory. The model is the domain in which F0 is used, not the mechanism by which it is computed. A domain of application is not a dependency.

The cepstrum's accepted definition computes the power spectrum via FFT, logs the magnitudes, and inverse-FTs them - the spectral input is a spectrum, not an STFT. STFT is one of several ways to obtain spectral estimates (cepstral analysis for pitch detection uses full-spectrum cepstrum, not windowed frames). Remove STFT and the cepstrum operates identically on an ordinary FFT spectrum. STFT is an alternative spectral source, not the mechanism of the transform itself - a substitutable input is not a dependency.
